result:
I fixed the label schema and review queue failure on SQL Server 2022 and older. The three related test files pass (368 tests) with the fix.

**The cause:** The lookup that finds an experiment's protected default label schema (`_ensure_default_label_schema` in `mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py`) filtered with `SqlLabelSchema.is_default.is_(True)`. On SQL Server that becomes `is_default IS 1`, which 2022 and older reject as a syntax error. Listing label schemas and loading review queue questions both go through this lookup, so both were broken.

**The fix:** I changed the filter to `SqlLabelSchema.is_default == sqlalchemy.true()`. On SQL Server this becomes `is_default = 1`. Other databases still get their normal true/1 check, so behavior there doesn't change. I also updated the comment above the query to explain why it isn't written with `.is_(True)`.

**Workspace-aware setup:** It runs this same method, so the one change covers both setups.

**Test:** You already had a test staged in `test_sqlalchemy_store_label_schemas.py`, `test_default_question_lookup_uses_mssql_compatible_boolean_predicate`, so I kept it rather than writing another. It builds the lookup query as SQL Server would see it and checks that it contains `is_default = 1` and not `IS 1`. It also checks that the default label schema is still found and marked protected. It runs with workspaces both off and on. Nothing was tested against a real SQL Server instance; the check is on the generated SQL.
